brand.tagline: Every civic district that covers your point in Iowa, and who represents you there.

head.title: What district am I in? Find your Iowa district — districtry
head.description: Click a point in Iowa — or search an address — and see your U.S. House, Iowa Senate, Iowa House and county, and who represents you.
head.og_description: Every civic district that covers a point in Iowa, and who holds it.
head.og_image_alt: districtry Iowa — every district that covers a point, and who represents it.
head.twitter_description: Click or search an Iowa address to see every district that covers it.

layers.label: U.S. House
layers.rank_note: Congressional districts — the largest districts a state carries below the state itself

source.answers: The U.S. House district covering the point, and the representative holding it.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Legislative, layer 0 (congressional districts), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app

source.people: congress-roster.json, rebuilt weekly by CI from the public-domain unitedstates/congress-legislators dataset — including each member's district office and Washington office.

layers.label: Iowa Senate District
layers.rank_note: 50 Senate districts, each the union of two whole House districts

source.answers: The Iowa Senate district covering the point, and the senator holding it.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Legislative, layer 1 (state upper chamber), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app

source.people: ia-senate-members.json, rebuilt weekly by CI — the Open States current-people export (name, party, e-mail) merged with each senator's own profile page at legis.iowa.gov (Capitol phone, and the Capitol's own address where the state publishes it).

layers.label: County
layers.rank_note: 99 counties, pre-built from TIGERweb; the fork's offline anchor layer

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — State_County, layer 1, pre-built for the state and shipped with the app

layers.label: Iowa House District
layers.rank_note: 100 House districts; two nest exactly inside each Senate district

source.answers: The Iowa House district covering the point, and the representative holding it.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Legislative, layer 2 (state lower chamber), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app

source.people: ia-house-members.json, rebuilt weekly by CI — the Open States current-people export (name, party, e-mail) merged with each representative's own profile page at legis.iowa.gov (Capitol phone, and the Capitol's own address where the state publishes it).

layers.label: County Supervisor District
layers.rank_note: The flagship layer: 270 features across 98 counties, PLANTYPE-aware (at-large / residence-district / single-member)

source.answers: The county supervisor district covering the point (where drawn), the county's election plan (at-large, residence-district-elected-countywide, or single-member district), and the board's size.

boundary.label: Iowa Legislature ArcGIS organization — CountySupervisorDistricts, pre-built for the state and shipped with the app (vintage 2024-01-30; licenseInfo not stated, attribution-only posture)
Black Hawk County's own hosted GIS — its adopted Senate File 75 plan (5 districts, vintage 2026-02-24), shipped in place of the state layer's stale pre-SF75 at-large row for this county alone

Story County's own site — states its SOS-approved Senate File 75 plan's facts (3 districts, populations, approval dates); no GIS service found, so the county ships as one county-level feature pending real district geometry

Johnson County's own site — states its SOS-approved Senate File 75 plan's facts (5 districts, ideal population); no GIS service found, so the county ships as one county-level feature pending real district geometry

source.people: No statewide roster of Iowa county supervisors exists (measured, research pass) — every card links the county's own board page instead of naming anyone. ia-county-board-directory.json (board size read back from the shipped geometry + the county's own official site from the Iowa State Association of Counties' member directory) supplies that link; Jones County carries no row in either file — it is entirely absent from the state's own aggregate (measured by name and by FIPS), a recorded gap rather than a guess.
source.applies: Iowa — 98 of 99 counties (Jones County is a recorded gap).

layers.label: School District (Unified)
layers.rank_note: 324 unified school districts, statewide — the only school-district tiling Iowa runs (TIGER's elementary/secondary layers measure zero)

source.answers: The unified school district covering the point.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — School, layer 0 (unified school districts), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 325 features, one dissolved into a neighbor to reconcile against the state's own current count (see the Dept. of Education witness below)

Iowa Dept. of Education — CurrentIowaSchoolDistricts (324 districts; Orient-Macksburg dissolved into Nodaway Valley for the 2026-2027 school year, ahead of TIGERweb's federal vintage), used only as a name-set witness the builder checks itself against, never as the geometry source

negative_point.note: inside Minnesota (near Albert Lea), north of the Iowa land border (~43.50) and inside permalink_gate's maxLat (43.70) so the point is still selectable

geometry.note: The whole-Iowa-state outline for the coverage wash (loadMetroOutline), dissolved from all 99 counties' TIGERweb State_County layer-1 geometry by ia/scripts/build_metro_outline.py (METRO_COUNTY_FIPS = every county; DISPATCH_COUNTY_FIPS empty — no layer is county-keyed yet). Iowa is 2-band coverage — no second, wider region file is needed yet (the WI #523 precedent for when one would be).
Every county, pre-built from TIGERweb State_County layer 1.
U.S. House districts, pre-built from TIGERweb Legislative layer 0.
Iowa Senate districts, pre-built by ia/scripts/build_legislative_boundaries.py (2,000-point agreement gate).
Iowa House districts, pre-built by ia/scripts/build_legislative_boundaries.py (2,000-point agreement gate).

Every county supervisor district across 98 of 99 counties (Jones County absent — a recorded gap), built by ia/scripts/build_ia_supervisor_districts.py: the state's own aggregate for 95 counties, Black Hawk's own hosted GIS (5 real districts), and Story/Johnson as one county-level TRANSITIONING feature each (5,000-in-state-point agreement gate).

Jones County's own boundary, extracted from state-counties.json by ia/scripts/build_ia_county_outline.py — the Data-gaps panel's map highlight for gap jones-county-supervisor. Referenced dynamically (built from the gap's county slug at runtime), never by a literal in index.html.

324 unified school districts, built by ia/scripts/build_ia_school_districts.py: TIGERweb's 325 dissolved (Orient-Macksburg into Nodaway Valley) and witnessed by name against the Dept. of Education's own current layer (2,000-point agreement gate).

rosters.note: U.S. House roster, refreshed weekly by update-ia-congress-roster.yml.
Senate roster from Open States ia.csv + legis.iowa.gov enrichment, refreshed weekly by update-ia-legislature-roster.yml; floor tolerates transient vacancies (50 seats).
House roster from Open States ia.csv + legis.iowa.gov enrichment, refreshed weekly by update-ia-legislature-roster.yml; floor tolerates transient vacancies (100 seats).

One row per county covered by ia-supervisor-districts.json: board size read back from the shipped geometry, plus the county's own official page (Iowa State Association of Counties' member directory) for the card's footer link. Built by ia/scripts/build_ia_county_board_directory.py; not a roster of people — Iowa publishes none statewide.
The Data gaps panel's content; one recorded gap (Jones County, absent from the county-supervisor source layer).

history_page.intro: districtry Iowa launched with the national tier: every county, both chambers of the Iowa Legislature, and Iowa's U.S. House delegation.

entries.title: Launched
entries.body: The national tier: county, U.S. House, Iowa Senate and Iowa House — four layers, statewide, each with a sourced boundary and (except county, identity-only by design) a weekly-refreshed officeholder roster. The flagship county-supervisor layer and the rest of the phase-1 roadmap follow in later PRs.
